title: "Hi Mum, I lost my phone" - that new-number text may be a scam
description:
Got a "Hi Mum, I lost my phone, this is my new number" text? Check before you pay.

Scammers message parents, often on WhatsApp, pretending to be their child on a new number. They chat first, then ask for money for an urgent bill, saying they can't get into their online banking.

On April 20, 2026, North Wales Police warned of a twist: texts that pretend to come from a parent who has lost their bank card, asking you to cover a bill.

In Australia, 82% of family impersonation scam reports in the first seven months of 2022 came from people over 55 (Scamwatch, ACCC).

Analyst note: a new number proves nothing. A new number plus an urgent money request is the whole scam.

Do this tonight:
1. Call the number already saved in your phone - don't reply in the same chat.
2. Ask something only they would know.
3. Never send money until you're sure who gets it. If you already paid, call your bank right away.

Sources
- Scamwatch / ACCC (Aug 23, 2022): https://www.scamwatch.gov.au/node/1065
- North Wales Police warning via Deeside.com (Apr 20, 2026): https://www.deeside.com/new-twist-on-hi-mum-scam-sees-criminals-impersonating-parents-in-text-messages/
- FBI IC3 PSA I-120324-PSA (Dec 3, 2024): https://www.ic3.gov/psa/2024/psa241203

Narration uses an AI voice (ElevenLabs). Research, script and fact-check by Securidge.
